tagline: A short road between stone fences into the Shaker village.
intro: The byway is the stretch of US 68 northeast of Harrodsburg that comes into the Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill, 1.2 miles on either side of the entrance. Along it runs one of the longest unbroken stretches of hand-laid stone fence in Kentucky.

The Shakers took their walls seriously. A visitor in 1857 reported that they had paid one hired man for twelve years to build them full-time, and that he had laid forty miles of them. The community lasted from 1805 to 1910, and the restoration began in 1961.

moments.title: Pleasant Hill
moments.text: By 1825 the village had large stone and brick dwellings, grassy lawns and stone walks, and by the early 1830s a horse-pumped water tower, believed to be the first in the state.

moments.title: Meeting House
moments.text: After the Shakers it served as an automotive garage, its floor, built to bear several hundred dancing brethren and sisters, proving strong enough for the cars.

moments.title: Trustee's Office
moments.text: Thomas Merton came over from the Abbey of Gethsemani in 1959 and wrote of its double winding stair going up to the clarity of a dome on the roof.
